intro: LeBron James is a 76er now, and yes, that actually happened. Meanwhile, Messi is out here dismantling World Cup competition one country at a time — ask Egypt how that went.

stories.headline: Messi Is Breaking the World Cup and Egypt Found Out the Hard Way
stories.body: Argentina trailed Egypt 2-0 before Messi scored his eighth goal of the tournament and Enzo Fernández buried a stoppage-time winner to complete the 3-2 comeback. Messi has now scored in nine consecutive World Cup matches for Argentina and leads the Golden Boot race — at this point it's less a tournament and more a highlight reel.

stories.headline: Mbappé Scores, Sets Up a Goal, and Promptly Scares Everyone by Limping Off
stories.body: France beat Morocco 2-0 in the quarter-finals in Boston, with Mbappé missing a penalty before delivering a sublime goal and an assist for Dembélé — then exiting in the 77th minute with an apparent injury. Deschamps now has a semi-final to prepare for and a fitness cloud over his best player.

stories.headline: Alexia Putellas to London City Lionesses Is the Biggest Women's Transfer Ever, Full Stop
stories.body: The two-time Ballon d'Or winner has signed with London City Lionesses in what is being called the most significant signing in the history of women's club football. Manchester City Women also added Niamh Charles from Chelsea on a three-year deal, so the WSL arms race this summer is very much real.

stories.headline: LeBron James Is a 76er Now, Because Why Not
stories.body: LeBron James has officially signed with the Philadelphia 76ers, ending his eight-year run with the Lakers and kicking off a record 24th NBA season with a new team. He reportedly wasn't interested until Boston shipped Jaylen Brown to Philly — so credit the Celtics for accidentally building LeBron's next contender.

stories.headline: Giannis Heads to Miami, Eastern Conference Chaos Ensues
stories.body: The Milwaukee Bucks have traded Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat, with Bucks leadership offering public goodbyes once the deal was done. The Eastern Conference now features Giannis in Miami, LeBron and Jaylen Brown in Philly, and Jalen Brunson recovering from wrist surgery in New York — someone's going to have a very bad April.

stories.headline: Kyle Lowry Hangs It Up After 20 Years
stories.body: Kyle Lowry has retired from the NBA, closing out a 20-year career highlighted by delivering Toronto its only championship in 2019. He leaves as the defining point guard of the Raptors era — and the guy Drake has to miss the most.

stories.headline: Muchová Saves Match Point, Gatekeeps Gauff Out of Wimbledon Final
stories.body: Karolina Muchová beat Coco Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6(12-10) in a tiebreak that had absolutely no business going that long, saving a match point along the way to reach her first Wimbledon final. Linda Nosková is waiting for her there after dispatching Marta Kostyuk 6-4, 6-4, setting up a final with zero former Wimbledon champions in it.

stories.headline: Djokovic Grinds Out Five-Set War to Set Up Sinner Semifinal
stories.body: Novak Djokovic beat Félix Auger-Aliassime 7-6, 3-6, 6-3, 6-7, 7-6 in a match that required two tiebreaks just to finish, booking his eighth consecutive Wimbledon semifinal where Jannik Sinner — who beat Jan-Lennard Struff in a relatively breezy three sets — is next up.

stories.headline: Mboko Out of Canadian Open as Knee Gives Way
stories.body: Victoria Mboko has withdrawn from the Canadian Open due to a knee injury, cutting her summer hard-court season short before it started.

stories.headline: Ducks Match Flyers' Monster $90M Offer Sheet, Keep Leo Carlsson
stories.body: Philadelphia threw a grenade at Anaheim by signing Leo Carlsson to a five-year, $90 million offer sheet — a deal that would've cost the Flyers four draft picks if the Ducks walked away. Anaheim matched it, keeping their franchise center and leaving Philly with nothing but a very expensive lesson.

stories.headline: Celebrini Signs the Richest Contract in NHL History
stories.body: Macklin Celebrini just became the highest-paid player in NHL history on an annual basis, locking up a record-setting deal with the San Jose Sharks. The Sharks also nabbed three first-round picks in the 2026 Draft, so apparently the rebuild is going just fine.

stories.headline: Bobrovsky Bolts to Toronto, Leafs Finally Have a Goalie
stories.body: Sergei Bobrovsky left Florida after three straight Stanley Cup Final runs and signed a $21 million deal with the Toronto Maple Leafs, giving them the proven playoff netminder they've been desperately searching for. The Panthers responded by trading for Jacob Markstrom within days, because panicking efficiently is still a skill.

stories.headline: Brissett Gets Paid: Cardinals Lock Up Their QB at $15.5 Million
stories.body: Jacoby Brissett ended his offseason contract standoff with Arizona, signing a one-year deal worth $15.5 million that can climb to $21 million with incentives. He's the guy in the desert — at least for now.

stories.headline: Shanahan Still Sidelined as 49ers Camp Opens Without Their Head Coach
stories.body: Kyle Shanahan missed the start of San Francisco's training camp while recovering from injuries sustained in a car accident earlier this month. Not exactly the vibe you want heading into a season with Super Bowl expectations.

stories.headline: Lions CB Terrion Arnold Hit With $1 Million Bond in Kidnapping and Assault Case
stories.body: A Florida judge set a $1 million bond for Detroit cornerback Terrion Arnold after charges stemming from a kidnapping and assault case. The Lions are going to have a lot more to worry about than pass coverage this summer.

stories.headline: Rays Shut Out Yankees Again, Now Own a Five-Game Cushion in the AL East
stories.body: Tampa Bay blanked New York 3-0 on Wednesday to push their AL East lead to five games, with the Rays sitting at 53-36 on the season. The Yankees are 50-41 and running out of room to breathe.

stories.headline: Trout's Back and Already Hitting Bombs, Because Of Course He Is
stories.body: Mike Trout came off the IL this week and immediately hit a two-run homer in his return. Meanwhile, Byron Buxton landed on the 10-day IL with a hip injury, because the baseball gods must maintain balance.

stories.headline: Ohtani Hits 300 Home Runs, Crow-Armstrong Makes History — Just Another Week in MLB
stories.body: Shohei Ohtani reached 300 career home runs this week while Pete Crow-Armstrong became the first 20/20 player in MLB this season. Justin Verlander also announced he's retiring after 2026, so the milestone energy was running high.

stories.headline: Norris Finally Breaks Through in Hungary While Antonelli Somehow Extends His Lead Anyway
stories.body: Lando Norris took McLaren's first win of the season at the Hungarian GP, holding off Verstappen and Antonelli for the top step. Antonelli finished third but still extended his championship lead — because of course he did.

stories.headline: Leclerc's Silverstone Win Was Great, But the Chaos Around It Won't Quit
stories.body: Charles Leclerc ended a nearly two-year win drought at the British GP, but the race finished under a safety car in scenes everyone's still arguing about, while Antonelli was hit with a controversial penalty after starting from pole and limping home in P16. Juan Pablo Montoya is now publicly demanding rule changes, which tells you everything about the temperature in the paddock.

stories.headline: Horner's Back in the Paddock and Already Talking About a Return
stories.body: Christian Horner made his first appearance inside the F1 paddock since being sacked as Red Bull team boss, saying any full comeback hinges on whether he can be a winner again. He's also writing a memoir about his 20 years at Red Bull, so the quiet exit is officially off the table.

stories.headline: 21-Year-Old Jackson Koivun Torches TPC Twin Cities, Beats Scheffler by Three
stories.body: Jackson Koivun shot a tournament-record 25-under 259 to claim his first PGA Tour title at the 3M Open, pocketing $1,584,000 and leaving world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler in second place — again. At 21, Koivun just became the most interesting name in golf overnight.

stories.headline: Scheffler Is Everywhere and Winning Nowhere: The Runner-Up Season Continues
stories.body: Scottie Scheffler has now finished second at both the Travelers Championship — where Viktor Hovland beat him in a Monday playoff — and the 3M Open, adding to a season full of near-misses despite holding the world No. 1 ranking. He's the best player in the world who keeps letting someone else grab the trophy.

stories.headline: Haeran Ryu Storms from 10 Back to Steal KPMG Women's PGA from Nelly Korda
stories.body: Haeran Ryu switched putters mid-tournament at Hazeltine and erased a 10-shot first-round deficit to claim her first major title at the KPMG Women's PGA Championship. Korda, still searching for another major, is now off to a rocky start at the Evian Championship as well.

stories.headline: NCAA Blows Up the Redshirt Era: Five Years to Play Five, No More Loopholes
stories.body: The NCAA officially replaced its tangled redshirt-and-waiver system with a clean five-seasons-in-five-years model, with the eligibility clock starting at first full-time enrollment or the year after a player turns 19. The goal is fewer 26-year-olds on college rosters — which, fair enough, probably should have happened before COVID made it a crisis.

stories.headline: Texas Tech's Brendan Sorsby Gets His Eligibility Back, Drops NCAA Lawsuit, and Won't Be Going to the NFL Supplemental Draft
stories.body: Sorsby sued the NCAA over a gambling-related eligibility ban, got a court injunction reinstating him for the 2026 season, then dropped the lawsuit entirely — all while the NFL quietly decided not to hold a supplemental draft anyway. A wild few weeks that somehow ended with him exactly where he started: a college quarterback.

stories.headline: Ohio State and Notre Dame Are Putting Corporate Logos on Their Jerseys for a Combined $37 Million a Year
stories.body: Ohio State inked a jersey patch deal with JPMorgan Chase worth roughly $17 million annually, while Notre Dame went one better with a SoFi patch deal at around $20 million per year. College football's "amateur" era is doing just fine, thanks.
